- ENT symptoms: 
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Denied

- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None reported.
- Allergies and current medications: 
  • Allergy – Amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).  
  • Medication – Etonogestrel implant (Implanon; dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • No regular or rescue medications.
- Social context: Lives with boyfriend; sexually active; contraception via implant.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: Normal per history; no stridor or dyspnea noted.
- Mental status/associated features: No light-headedness, no syncope.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (teleconsultation).
- Accompaniment: Patient was alone during video call.

Assessment:
- No ENT pathology identified. Presentation consistent with lower abdominal pain and nausea of unclear etiology (possible gastrointestinal, gynecologic, or urinary-tract source). ENT involvement not indicated at this stage.

Plan:
- Immediate action: Advised face-to-face GP assessment today for physical examination, pregnancy test, and further investigations.
- Patient counselling:  
  • Seek urgent care if symptoms worsen, develop light-headedness, or any new concerning features.  
  • No specific ENT red flags currently; advised to seek emergency help if any throat swelling, difficulty breathing, or voice change occurs.
- Follow-up: GP appointment arranged; no ENT follow-up required unless new ENT symptoms develop.
